title: Move customized Identity UI off Bootstrap 4
goal: Keep customized sign-in pages rendering when upgrading Identity UI by selecting Bootstrap 5 and migrating the affected markup, styles and published assets.

packageAssets: Matching locked Identity.UI/store/SQLite packages, with actual ZIPs, selected net10.0/net11.0 assets and loaded native SQLite recorded separately. Package static web assets are published under /Identity; no CDN is used.
providers: Real Identity EF SQLite store; ephemeral fixture data protection and two fictional local accounts. No third-party provider or real message transport.
platforms: Qualified execution: Windows x64 only. No NativeAOT, trimming or other OS/native-provider execution claim.
renderingModes: Published server-rendered Razor Pages, local Bootstrap CSS and authored CSS; actual Chromium login and server-validation rendering. No Blazor or JavaScript validation claim.
prerequisites: Existing customized Identity UI plus its original Razor/layout/CSS assets. Restore all locked packages before offline use; a real browser is required to check presentation after publishing.
constraints: Changing the property selects packaged UI/assets; it does not rewrite customized Razor or CSS. Only the bounded form/checkbox/button selectors shown here are migrated.

Bootstrap4 still builds in the measured RC2 package but produces an obsolete-support warning. Do not suppress that warning as a migration. Remove BOTH IdentityUIFrameworkVersion and an inherited IdentityDefaultUIFramework when choosing defaults. An empty GLOBAL MSBuild property is not equivalent to removing it.

Keep existing confirmation/lockout/session policy and antiforgery. This fixture uses PasswordSignInAsync, requires confirmed accounts, validates local return URLs and checks denied/allowed fresh principals. The form is not a complete production Identity replacement: add the application's existing 2FA, recovery, external-login and accessibility requirements when applicable.

Fixture-only accounts, ephemeral keys, EnsureCreated database and HTTP loopback are test infrastructure; use production key storage, HTTPS, schema migrations and legitimate account lifecycle services. The browser checks are one Windows Chromium viewport, not all assistive technology or mobile proof.
stabilityLimitations: Exact reproduction uses SDK10.0.402 / framework10.0.13 / C#14 versus SDK11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105 / framework11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105 / C#15. These are tested pins, not minimum supported versions. RC2 is not actual-GA proof. The exact eight approved .NET10 foundations, stable identities, PIN-959/PIN-963/PIN-964 and unrelated Human gates remain unchanged.

evidence.scope: Both actual dependency sets compile. Published HTTP checks cover custom layout/CSS, missing-token 400, validation, denied unconfirmed account, allowed confirmed account and rejected external return URL. Actual package targets produce the Bootstrap4 warning. Both explicit5 and property-removal copies publish and execute. Chromium152/Electron44 on Windows at1280x800 rendered login and validation for all three publishes: loaded local stylesheets, labeled inputs, 480px panels, 414px buttons, readable red error text and no horizontal overflow; screenshots were visually inspected. This is server validation, not unobtrusive/client JavaScript proof.
